title: Translate the customer database's failures at the service boundary

blocks.text: The support dashboard looks customers up through `CustomerService`. It shows "no such customer" for `UnknownCustomerException`, "try again later" for `CustomerStoreException`, and sends anything else to the error tracker as a bug. The repository underneath is JDBC code, and the dashboard team doesn't want to know about `SQLException`.

Three complaints arrived after the last release. Agents who mistype a customer id are told to try again later, and do, for minutes. When the database does fail, the log says only "cannot load customer", and on-call can't tell a timeout from a full connection pool. And a mapping bug introduced in the repository last week showed up on the dashboard as a database outage, so nobody opened a bug for it.
Write `find(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/CustomerService.java` so that each of the three reaches the right place. About eight lines.

cases.says: a customer the repository finds is returned
an SQLException from the repository reaches the caller as CustomerStoreException
the CustomerStoreException carries the repository's SQLException as its cause
an id with no customer is reported as UnknownCustomerException, not as a store failure
an unchecked exception from the repository reaches the caller unchanged

origin.section: Translate Exceptions at a Layer Boundary, and Keep the Cause

concepts: The translated exception keeps the lower layer's exception as its cause, so the log still shows what failed.
A service translates only the lower layer's own failure type, in a try holding only the call, so its own exceptions and bugs are not reported as store failures.
